texts.preamble: Raj Kumar Sharma vs Food Safety Officer on 25 July, 2024 In The Court Of Mr. Vimal Kumar Yadav Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/ Principal District & Sessions Judge, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Fsat No. 03/2023 Cnr No. Dlnd01-001814-2023
texts.facts: Both the above referred appeals are taken up together being outcome of same order/adjudication. The appellant was ordered to pay a penalty of Rs. 1 lac each (in case of Raj Kumar Sharma, FSAT No.03/2023) and Rs.50,000/- each (in case of Sharwan Kumar, FSAT No.01/2023). 2. While assailing the order of the Adjudicating Officer, it is contended on behalf of Raj Kumar Sharma that he is not the manufacturer of the Dhaniya Powder, sample of which was bought on 11.12.2014 by the Food Safety Officer, from the shop of Raj Kumar Sharma of M/s. Shimla General Store, 1A, Sewa Nagar Market, New Delhi-03. The said Dhaniya Powder was in a sealed packet and four such sealed packets were taken. Those samples were further subjected to analysis and examination by the Food Safety Officer from NABL accredited FSAT No. 03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.2 of 9 laboratory, where on examination it was found that sample was sub-standard since total ash on dry basis exceeded the prescribed maximum limit of 7.0% by weight. The Designated Officer was provided with the case file including the Food Analyst's report and Food Safety Officer's report, and after obtaining the sanction for prosecution under Section 36 (3) (e) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, an application was moved before the Adjudicating Officer for summoning, trial and punishment to the accused persons which ultimately resulted into the impugned order. 3. There are two set of appellants, one is the grocery shop owner Raj Kumar Sharma, from whose shop M/s. Shimla General Store, sample of Dhaniya Powder in question was bought/lifted by the Food Safety Officer and the other is the manufacturer, which is a partnership firm having two partners. The stand of former is to the effect that he was selling a sealed and packed item manufactured by the other set of persons i.e. Krishna Masala Company, whereas latter has washed off its hands by asserting that the goods in question were not supplied by them and that they have no concern with this spurious/adulterated Dhaniya Powder, as no document, receipt, supply order etc. could be produced on record to connect them with sampled article. 4. The Adjudicating Officer, who, in the impugned order held both set of persons i.e. Raj Kumar Sharma on one hand and Krishna Masala Company and its partners on the other hand responsible for the adulteration and after holding them FSAT No. 03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.3 of 9 responsible, levied penalty of Rs. 1 lakh on Raj Kumar Sharma and Rs.50,000/- each on the partners of Krishna Masala Company.
texts.arguments: 5. It is contended on behalf of appellant Krishan Masala Company that there is no evidence on record which may reflect that item in question i.e. Dhaniya Powder was either manufactured or sold by them to Raj Kumar Sharma, FBO-cum- proprietor. In such circumstances, merely having address Raj Kumar Sharma vs Food Safety Officer on 25 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86882483/ 2 on the label cannot be enough to link and connect the appellant Krishan Masala Company and its partners with the adulterated Dhaniya Powder. There is no investigation on this aspect and therefore, when the shop owner, who has failed to produce any document, which may have even remotely indicated that the "Dhaniya Powder" in question was supplied by Krishna Masala Company, then in these circumstances, the appellant Krishna Masala Company and its partners cannot be held responsible in any manner so far as, the instant matter is concerned. Ld. Counsel for appellant Krishna Masala Company has placed reliance on the judgment titled as M/s Parakh Food Limited Vs. State of AP [(2008 (1) (FAC 150)] and asserted that nobody can be prosecuted merely on the basis of label declaration of address of the manufactures. However, the observations in the judgment are in a different context and not about prosecuting the manufacturer on the basis of address alone. 6. On the other hand, Ld. counsel for appellant Raj Kumar Sharma has sought to take advantage of Section 80 of the Act but in the absence of any document, which may connect the FSAT No. 03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.4 of 9 product in question to the Appellant Krishna Masala Company, the arguments remain bald assertions, having no substance and therefore, appellant Raj Kumar Sharma cannot get any advantage. 7. 10. Reference can also be made to Judgments in cases titled as Kishore Kumar Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, [(2009) (2) FAC 333], R.K. Aggarwal vs. State of Haryana and Anr., Criminal Misc. No.5943 of 1992 dated 29.10.1992 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court and Mohinder Kumar Vs. State of Haryana, [(2004) (1) FAC 65].
